name: Bernie Sanders
kicker: Independent senator from Vermont · Ran for president in 2016 and 2020
dates: Born 1941; elected to the Senate in 2006
briefing: Bernie Sanders grew up in Brooklyn, protested segregation as a college student in Chicago, and moved to Vermont, where he was elected mayor of Burlington in 1981 by just ten votes. He served in the U.S. House from 1991 to 2007, won a Senate seat in 2006, and became the longest-serving independent in the history of Congress. A self-described democratic socialist, he ran for the Democratic presidential nomination in 2016 and 2020.

tossups.p: This politician was elected mayor of Burlington by just ten votes in 1981, and he later recorded a folk album called _We Shall Overcome_ while serving in that job. He then won Vermont’s only seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in 1990.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this independent senator from Vermont who ran for president in 2016 and 2020.

tossups.p: As a student at the University of Chicago, this future politician joined the Congress of Racial Equality and was arrested in 1963 at a protest against school segregation. That summer, he also attended the March on Washington.
tossups.r: Decades later, he represented Vermont in Congress. For 10 points, name this self-described democratic socialist who ran for president in 2016.

tossups.p: In the 1970s, this politician ran unsuccessfully for governor and for U.S. senator as a candidate of the Liberty Union Party, a small third party in Vermont. In 1991, he helped found the Congressional Progressive Caucus.
tossups.r: He later became the longest-serving independent in the history of Congress. For 10 points, name this senator from Vermont.

tossups.p: In December 2010, this senator spoke on the Senate floor for more than eight hours against a deal to extend tax cuts first passed under George W. Bush, and the speech was later published as a book. He had won his Senate seat in 2006, replacing the retiring Jim Jeffords.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this independent from Vermont who ran for the Democratic presidential nomination in 2016.

tossups.p: As chair of the Senate Veterans’ Affairs Committee, this senator worked with John McCain on a 2014 law that let some veterans see private doctors when Veterans Affairs hospitals had long waits. From 2023 to 2025, he chaired the Senate committee on health, education, labor, and pensions.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Vermont senator who sought the Democratic nomination for president in 2016 and 2020.

tossups.p: In February 2016, this son of a Jewish immigrant from Poland became the first Jewish candidate to win a U.S. presidential primary, beating his main rival in New Hampshire by more than twenty percentage points.
tossups.r: His supporters used the slogan “Feel the Bern.” For 10 points, name this Vermont senator who lost the 2016 Democratic nomination to Hillary Clinton.

tossups.p: The comedian Larry David played this politician on _Saturday Night Live_, and the PBS show _Finding Your Roots_ later revealed that the two men are distant cousins. Both men grew up in Brooklyn, New York.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this independent senator from Vermont who ran for president in 2016 and 2020.

tossups.p: At Joe Biden’s inauguration in 2021, a photo of this senator sitting with his arms and legs crossed in hand-knit mittens, made by a Vermont teacher, became a popular internet meme. He used the image to sell sweatshirts that raised money for charities in his state.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Vermont senator who lost the 2020 Democratic nomination to Biden.

tossups.p: After his first presidential campaign, this politician wrote the book _Our Revolution_, which shares its name with a political group founded by his supporters. His second presidential campaign used the slogan “Not me. Us.”
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Vermont senator who sought the Democratic nomination in 2016 and 2020.

tossups.p: At the 2016 Democratic National Convention, this candidate asked that Hillary Clinton be nominated by acclamation, ending a primary race in which he had won more than twenty states. He then campaigned for her against Donald Trump.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Vermont senator who also ran for president in 2020.

tossups.p: In 2020, this candidate won the most votes in the New Hampshire primary and won the Nevada caucuses, but he ended his campaign that April as his main rival built a large lead in delegates.
tossups.r: He then endorsed that rival, Joe Biden. For 10 points, name this independent senator from Vermont.

tossups.p: This politician wrote about serving as an independent in Congress in the 1997 book _Outsider in the House_. When he won his first House race in 1990, he became the first independent elected to the House in about forty years.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Vermont politician who later sought the Democratic presidential nomination twice.

tossups.p: As chair of the Senate Budget Committee from 2021 to 2023, this senator helped pass the American Rescue Plan, a COVID-19 relief law, through a process called budget reconciliation. Although he was elected as an independent, he joined the Democrats’ caucus in the Senate.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Vermont senator who ran for president in 2016 and 2020.

tossups.p: This politician grew up in Brooklyn, New York, the son of a paint salesman who had immigrated from Poland, and he studied at Brooklyn College before transferring to the University of Chicago. In the late 1960s, he moved to Vermont.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Vermont senator who called for “Medicare for All” in two runs for president.

tossups.p: During his 2016 campaign, this candidate often said that his average campaign donation was $27, and he relied on small donors instead of a super PAC. He called for overturning the _Citizens United_ decision, which allowed unlimited independent political spending by corporations and labor unions.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Vermont senator who lost the 2016 Democratic nomination to Hillary Clinton.

trap.title: Which progressive senator?
trap.body: Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren were both senators who ran for the 2020 Democratic nomination and both supported “Medicare for All,” so policy clues can fit either one. Sanders is an independent from Vermont; Warren is a Democrat from Massachusetts and a former Harvard law professor who first proposed the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. A different Sanders, Sarah Huckabee Sanders, was White House press secretary under Donald Trump and was elected governor of Arkansas in 2022.
trap.fix: Vermont, Burlington, the Liberty Union Party, or “democratic socialist” means Bernie Sanders. Massachusetts, Harvard Law, or the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau means Warren. Give the last name, because “Bernie” alone only earns a prompt.
